method: Every URL cited in data/rings.json, data/sellers.json and data/gold-price.json was opened again in this session on 2026-10-22. Each asserted value was compared against the text the page returned. A value that could not be found on the page was deleted or downgraded to unverified; a value that contradicted the page was corrected; a contradiction found on the page itself was raised as a flag.

passes.name: Fact pass
passes.what: For every row, each stored number and quote was searched for in the freshly fetched page text.
passes.result: 22/22 rows re-read; 9 rows corrected; 3 rows added.

passes.name: Request pass
passes.what: Checked that every row's product URL returns the product it claims to be — not a redirect to something else, not a sold-out placeholder, not a dead link.
passes.result: 1 redirect (R17), 1 sold-out/back-order state (R18), 1 identifier mismatch (R10), 0 dead links.

passes.name: Internet pass
passes.what: Each cited URL was opened rather than trusted: host checked against the seller's own domain, and the exact wording quoted.

passes.name: Hallucination pass
passes.what: Deliberately hostile re-read: any figure that felt plausible but was not literally on the page was removed. This is what caught the 'white/rose gold & platinum also offered' phrases on five Blue Nile rows and two Mejuri rows.
passes.result: 7 metal-option claims deleted; 1 price basis corrected; 1 temporary provenance flag retired.

passes.name: Third re-verification pass (session arena/699d8e05-gold3)
passes.what: Re-opened 47 official URLs live across Datasets A and B to hunt transplanted claims and dead links.
passes.result: Caught Wilson's 3% cancellation fee transplanted onto Sarraf (RET7/F15), 2 dead policy URLs (SRC1), wrong Sarraf email (F19), Ross-Simons & Catbird return policies filled (POL1 closed for both), Aurate 5.5-8.5g range & Exchange-Only Final Sale notice recorded (F13/F14).

discrepancies.what: Title/spec say 18K White Gold; the same page's description says 14k yellow gold.
Product URL redirects to a different product path; page content still matches the ring.
8.30 g is stated to be the weight of a size 10 ring, while sizes 3-16 are sold.
One weight line covers both 14k gold and 950 platinum options.
Weights are explicitly approximate, with a stated ±5% tolerance.
Product page says non-returnable and exchange-only, while the brand's general policy advertises 30-day returns.
Costco's official policy lists precious metals as non-refundable.
Product page callout states '9k Solid Gold' (below US 10K threshold) while bullet list states '10k solid yellow gold', and cash refunds expire after 14 days.
Trust badge advertises 'Free 1-Year Resizing' while Product Details states 'resizing is not available for this ring' (and Band Width selector prints '2 ct. tw.').
Sarraf's About page limits 30-day returns to 'non-engraved items', while its Returns page accepts engraved rings minus non-refundable $25 engraving / $50 finish fees.
Automic Gold product page states '4-8 business days' in the buy box and '1-2 weeks' (2-3 weeks engraved) in Shipping & Returns.
Automic Gold advertises a 30-day return window but its refund policy states 'To avoid a restocking fee, please mail your items within 14 days.'

site_defects.what: The dashboard's 'gold value by karat' table squared the melt value: it iterated the melt dict as if it were the fineness table, so 10K printed 5394.3% fineness and $6,983.75/g instead of 41.67% and $53.94/g.

site_defects.fix: All four pages are now generated statically from data/sellers.json, data/rings.json and data/standards.json by scripts/build_site.py, with no client-side dependency. Declared in the build so a regenerate cannot reintroduce it.

site_defects.what: A category intro quoted a "$6,000+" threshold that appears in no data file — a prose number presented as fact.
site_defects.fix: Reworded to a qualitative description; the page now prints only figures that come from data.

site_defects.what: The page was titled 'All verified listings' and its description said 'every verified solid gold ring listing', but it renders dataset A only (19 of the 41 listings the site carries). A reader could reasonably think the other 22 do not exist. Why it matters: An over-broad claim about completeness is a correctness problem even when every rendered value is sourced.
site_defects.fix: Retitled 'Dataset A: all verified listings' and added a scope box stating the count it renders and linking the combined list of 41. Guard: render-test.js asserts the scope box and both counts are present on rings.html.
site_defects.found_by: This session's own defect hunt: after every data change the site is re-read looking for claims it cannot support — here, a title promising more than the page renders, and two counts typed by hand.

site_defects.what: Two counts were typed into the generator as prose and never recomputed: a link list said '7 sellers' and the combined page's description said '28 listings across 9 sellers'. The site actually carries 41 listings across 12 sellers. Why it matters: Hand-typed counts are the same class of error as a hand-typed price: they drift silently as data is added and no source is ever checked.
site_defects.fix: Both strings now interpolate the computed METRICS values; they cannot drift again. Guard: A grep for a digit followed by ' listings'/' sellers' in scripts/build_site.py must return no literal counts outside f-strings (checked in this pass by hand; audit.py re-derives the totals from data).
